classes.name: Open water
classes.signature: Calm water reflects the pulse away from the radar, so the lake is among the darkest surfaces in HH and HV. Wind can roughen the surface and brighten it a little. At L-band smooth dry fields can be nearly as dark, so water is mapped from the connected lake shape, not from brightness alone.

classes.name: Built-up
classes.signature: Walls and the ground beside them act as corner reflectors that send the pulse straight back (double bounce), so HH is very bright. HV stays much lower, which gives the lowest HV:HH ratio of all types. Isolated farm buildings show up as bright points on the plain.

classes.name: Trees, shrub and rugged slopes
classes.signature: Leaves and branches scatter the pulse in many directions (volume scattering), which raises HV the most of all land types. Slopes facing the radar look bright in both channels. Tall crops and tree plots on the plain can fall in this type too.

classes.name: Changing fields
classes.signature: HV changed strongly between June and September, as it does when a crop grows (more volume scattering) or is harvested or ploughed (less). These are the fields with the most activity in the season. Which crop it is cannot be told from the radar alone.

classes.name: Rough dry ground and fields
classes.signature: Rough soil, stones and sparse plants send part of the pulse back (rough surface scattering), so HH and HV are medium. Little change from June to September. Found on dry fields of the plain and on stony ridges.

classes.name: Smooth bare ground and dry fields
classes.signature: Smooth dry soil reflects most of the pulse away, so HH and HV are low, close to calm water. Little change from June to September, which fits fallow or harvested land. The optical photo shows most of this type as bright bare soil.

areas.name: Bin El Ouidane reservoir
areas.description: The reservoir on the El Abid river and its shore.

context.fact: Bin El Ouidane dam is on the El Abid river, was built in 1949-1953 and irrigates about 69,500 ha of the Beni Moussa and Tadla plains.
ORMVAT selected a bid to modernise the Beni Moussa irrigation canals, which are supplied by Bin El Ouidane. The selection is subject to appeal.
